bio: Etienne Mason, known professionally as MAYSUN, is a composer and sound artist whose work transforms physical spaces into immersive sound environments.

Centered around modular systems, DIY electronics, and cyclical processing, he develops adaptable sound structures that interact with and reshape the contexts they inhabit. Blurring the lines between site-responsive installations and performance, his practice creates moments where sound, the room, and the listener become inseparable. Working with feedback circuits and spatial distribution, he creates the conditions for that participation.

MAYSUN is a NEW INC Y13 Extended Realities Member, a 2026 NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellow in Digital/Electronic Arts and was awarded a 2025-2026 microgrant from Rhizome. He was a selected participant in the New Amsterdam Composers Lab 2025 and completed a 2024 ITP/IMA Fellowship at New York University.
statement: MAYSUN explores how spatial audio, environmental sound, technology, and emotional resonance combine to create immersive experiences.

Working with custom electronics and distributed processing, he creates spatial audio systems that treat the site as a sound source. Microphones capture ambient sound, movement, conversation, silence. That audio is processed through granular effects, time manipulation, and feedback circuits, then redistributed through the space. The room hears itself and responds.
His systems are portable and site-specific. Each element shapes the sound differently. No two installations sound the same as no two environtments are the same.

This approach emerged from years of touring, recording spaces, and processing audio through physical environments. The most interesting sounds come from letting the space participate. His role is to build the conditions for that participation.

Current work involves a set of custom instruments, each extending how sound moves through physical space. The technology serves the room. Together they create immersive environments that respond to what is present.
